newsitem.title: USA: Continental, Delta get Brazil routes.
newsitem.headline: Continental, Delta get Brazil routes.

text.p: The U.S. Transportation Department on Friday said it had tentatively awarded Continental Airlines Inc and Delta Air Lines Inc rights to serve Brazil.

It said in a release it had selected Continental to serve Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro with daily non-stop flights from Newark, New Jersey, and Delta for daily non-stops to Sao Paulo from Atlanta with flights originating in Cincinnati.
The department said the U.S.-Brazil market is the largest U.S.-South America market, generating over two million passengers a year for U.S. and foreign carriers.
American Airlines, a unit of AMR, and United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp, already serve that market under a bilateral accord that allows four carriers.
The release said Tower Air was also seeking authority to enter the market and American wanted to increase its presence there.
The department is allowing for a 10-day comment period before making its decision final.
